verdicts.why: The note keeps to the overuse gloss - 'met everywhere' is the overfamiliarity the gloss names, the fault is explicitly 'the same overuse' threadbare and shopworn register as damage, the comparison checks against those two notes, the example fits, and -1 is plausible for the mildest-sounding member; the 'ordinariness' wording is the word's own flavour of the fault rather than a slide into the 'completely ordinary and unremarkable' sense, since that sense carries no fault at all.

The note explicitly keeps 'the overuse' as what happened and describes only how the word colours it (as age rather than as someone's running it into the ground), which is a force-and-flavour claim read off the word itself, the hackneyed comparison checks against the hackneyed note's 'run into the ground', there is no origin or frequency claim, the example fits, and -1 suits a word that lays the blame on time.

For a transparent 'smelling of X' compound the only thing the word does is pin the smell to a source, and the note positions it on exactly that axis (a wood, not a spice, fruit or sweet; the tree rather than a resin), the balsam-scented comparison checks against that note's 'the resin rather than the tree', no evaluation is smuggled in, and 0 is right for the gloss.

The warm/cool contrast is a fact about the spices, but the note says so in the same breath and assigns the word only what it does - identify the smell flatly - so it does not describe the thing instead of the word; the mint-scented and clove-scented comparisons check against those notes, and 0 fits the gloss.

The note stays with the feeling the gloss describes - depth of being brought low through shame or wounded pride - rather than sliding into the 'suffering shame' loss-of-standing synset, its 'no hand required' clause matches the gloss's own agentless example, the mortified comparison checks against that note's 'unbearable rather than merely awkward', and -2 sits plausibly between embarrassed and disgraced.
